items.title: Prospective Life Cycle Optimization of Carbon Capture and Storage/Utilization (CCS/CCU) Supply Chains in the Cement Industry
items.summary: The title indicates a prospective life-cycle optimisation study of CCS and CCU supply chains serving the cement industry. The abstract is not yet available.
items.why_it_matters: Cement is a core capture source in Nordic CCS chains (e.g. Brevik, Aalborg Portland); a combined life-cycle and supply-chain optimisation model is directly comparable to network-design work on capture-transport-storage chains.

items.title: Beyond Construction: The Platform Effect of Environmental Infrastructure in Carbon Capture and Storage
items.summary: The paper presents a replicable, multi-scalar IMPLAN-based framework to analyse the economic effects of a proposed CCS facility in a U.S. Gulf Coast county with a deep-water port. It separately examines sequestration field construction, pipeline system development, annual operations and on-site capture installations, and assesses impacts at local, regional and state level.
items.why_it_matters: Splitting regional economic effects by chain component (pipeline, storage field, capture, operations) offers a template for valuing port-based CCS hub infrastructure beyond the construction phase.
